propositions: Pytest basetemp removal fails on macOS when snapshot-producing tests leave read-only .rebar/run_snapshots directories with 0444/0555 permissions beneath basetemp.
Cleanup is owned only by a module-local fixture in test_snapshot.py, so snapshot producers in other test modules recreate the non-removable basetemp condition.
The existing snapshot._rmtree_writable seam successfully removes read-only snapshot trees by restoring writable permissions before deletion, but it is not invoked during shared pytest teardown.

Moving the exact .rebar/run_snapshots teardown rule from test_snapshot.py into an autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py will centralize cleanup ownership at the shared lifecycle boundary and cover all snapshot-producing test modules.

Production snapshots must remain non-writable during test execution; only the residual .rebar/run_snapshots roots below test-owned tmp_path are made writable and removed during shared teardown, leaving adjacent temp content untouched.
